extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, patent examiners, and law students studying re-issue doctrine
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and standards governing when and how an issued U.S. patent may be amended by re-issue: the permissible grounds, required state of mind (inadvertence/accident/mistake vs fraud), limits on added matter, and procedural/interpretive guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible grounds for re-issue
rubrics_metrics.description: The act confers the privilege of a re-issue whenever the Description or the Claim is inexact or incomplete, or when the Claim is broader than the actual invention, provided the error has arisen from inadvertence, accident, or mistake, and without any fraudulent or deceptive intention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the statutory core: re-issue is available to correct inexact/incomplete description or claims that overreach the inventor's actual invention, but only if the error was non-fraudulent and unintentional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sole object of a re-issue
rubrics_metrics.description: The sole object of a re-issue is to so amend an imperfect existing patent that it may disclose and protect the patentable subject-matter which it was the purpose of that patent to secure to its inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Re-issue is an amendment of an existing patent, not the grant of a new patent; it must be confined to the invention the patentee attempted to describe and claim in the original patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent must be existing and imperfect (not void or expired)
rubrics_metrics.description: The original patent must be an existing patent; a patent void ab initio (e.g., issued on a false oath of citizenship or an improper joint patent for a sole invention) is not an existing patent and cannot be re-issued. An expired patent cannot be re-issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the patent is void on its face or expired, remedy must be sought by application for new letters-patent, not by re-issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Errors amendable are errors of statement, not of subject-matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Defects amendable by re-issue are defects of statement in the Description or Claim (inexactness or incompleteness) and not defects of the patent's substantive subject-matter (i.e., you cannot, by re-issue, create rights to a different invention or new subject-matter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Re-issue corrects how the invention was described/claimed, not to appropriate different principles, later developments, or distinct inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement of inadvertence/accident/mistake and prohibition of fraud
rubrics_metrics.description: The defect or insufficiency must have arisen through inadvertence, accident, or mistake, and without any fraudulent or deceptive intention. A defective or insufficient statement purposely inserted with intent to deceive is regarded as fraud and is not amendable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions given: 'inadvertence' = want of attention; 'mistake' = want of knowledge; 'accident' = circumstances beyond inventor's control. Statements made voluntarily with knowledge/attention are not inadvertent and typically cannot be corrected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Office (and courts) determine inadvertence/fraud; evidence may defeat re-issue
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Office is to judge inadvertence, accident, or mistake on a re-issue application; where incompleteness is apparent from comparing Description and Claim, or where unreasonable delay or application history shows no inadvertence, courts treat that as conclusive evidence the inventor intended exclusion and will invalidate a re-issue attempting to reclaim it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unreasonable delay, clear discrepancy between description and claim at grant, or application history can be used as evidence that the defect was not inadvertent and bar re-issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-issue must be confined to the original invention as of original filing/date
rubrics_metrics.description: A re-issue cannot cover more than the original invention as determined by the state of the art at the date of the first patent; it cannot embrace any invention other than that which the patentee had fully invented and the government had endeavored to protect by the original patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This bars claiming later-developed applications, distinct inventions, different principles, or broader subject-matter that were not part of the patentee's original invention and understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cannot introduce new matter or different principle or different form not in original invention
rubrics_metrics.description: A re-issue cannot introduce a different principle though it was known when the original patent was obtained, nor can it claim other forms or devices which are not part of the original invention; antecedent improvements or other forms outside original limits cannot be embraced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even knowledge existing at the time of original patent does not permit a re-issue to claim a different principle or form unless that principle/form was part of the invention the patentee actually claimed or sufficiently described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits as to partially operative patents and parts of inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent may be valid and operative as to one invention or part and invalid/inoperative as to another; re-issue is available to correct defects so the patent can protect the invention the original patent attempted to secure, but only for those parts conceived, perceived, and practically operative at the time of the original application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where an invention has separable parts or steps, re-issue may correct defects related to the part(s) that were actually part of the original invention, but cannot be used to claim independent parts not embraced originally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of voluntary or willful drafting choices
rubrics_metrics.description: If a statement in the Description or Claim was made voluntarily with knowledge and attention (not through inadvertence/accident/mistake), the inventor is guilty of negligence or fraud and ought not to be permitted to amend; an intentionally obscure or overly broad Claim is fraudulent and void.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voluntary omissions or narrow drafting that exclude matter will generally preclude correction by re-issue — the inventor may be treated as having abandoned such matter or reserved it for a separate patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extent and form of allowable amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: When allowable, the amendment by re-issue can be made in any form and to any extent that may be necessary to render the patent effective for the protection of the original invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Re-issue can add omitted matter (if proved to have been part of the original invention and omitted by inadvertence), narrow claims, or restate claims more precisely — but always within the original invention's boundaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to claim or describe matter outside the original invention is not a defect
rubrics_metrics.description: No patent can be invalid or inoperative by reason of its failure to describe and claim matter lying outside the limits of the invention which was conceived and reduced to practice and which the government was asked to protect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intervening inventions, later developments, or aspects not reduced to practice before the original application date are beyond scope and do not furnish a basis for re-issue.
